en: The Hymn to the Lord of Añjanaśaila
With his hair standing on end, he worships the lady between his arms— she who is the merit for the eyes of the world and who fulfills all desires;
once again upon the mountain of the bull, he gazes upon her who possesses the luster of a blooming blue lotus.
May I experience that Puruṣa whose eyes are as broad as lotus petals. || 1 ||
To the one whose innate friendship is an ocean of boundless compassion-nectar, who is the primordial being of sincere affection and shoreless, excellent conduct,
a mass of bliss with a retinue consisting of pure devotion;
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
With copper-hued feet, clad in pure golden garments, with conch and discus shining upon his full shoulders and arms,
his face filled with wonder and his sidelong glances imbued with abundant compassion—
I worship Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain. || 3 ||
Possessing a physical form composed of extraordinary limbs, having ascended to the bloom of youth while not yet losing his princely character,
and endowed with a radiant splendor that transcends the reach of speech and mind.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain. || 4 ||
It possesses all fragrances arising from the space of hope;
it relishes the nature of all easily accessible flavors;
and it possesses an excellence of touch through the bliss attainable by embracing.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain. || 5 ||
He was displaying his power of vision to those whose eyes were extremely constricted,
making all who were deaf by nature hear,
and causing the multitude of those who were mute and bowed down on every side to speak.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
He was making the excessively swift run like that of the wind, causing the lame to leap with arms reaching down to their knees— oh,
how wonderful!— and restoring others to life who had been decapitated.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
He who makes those destitute of wealth from birth appear as if they possessed flaming hair; he who makes even the ignorant appear like the Teacher of the Thirty-three Gods;
he who instantly renders even a barren mortal fruitful.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
With bracelets bound upon his arms as a sign of being the refuge for all, a helper in times of distress who forgives the transgressions of those who bow before him,
and surrounded by a circle of sages languid with the bliss of proximity to Śambhu—
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
His feet, adorned with anklets, rest upon a lotus-seat; his shanks are long and rounded, encircled by hero-bands;
his pair of knees are marvelous, and his thighs are incomparable pillars.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
Whose navel is the cause of the entire universe with its revolving depths;
whose inner apartments are the play-palaces within the intervals of his outstretched arms; and who possesses four arms adorned with ornaments made of jewels.
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain. || 11 ||
With cheeks radiant from jeweled earrings hanging from his shoulders, with lips as sweet as bandhujīva flowers reflecting the rays of his smile,
and with a long nose eager for the fragrance of his lotus-like face—
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain. || 12 ||
With a vertical sectarian mark (*ūrdhvapuṇḍra*) shimmering on his forehead like the light of a half-moon,
with a face beautiful with swaying dark and curly locks of hair,
and wearing a great crown with a crest-jewel that radiates beams of light;
I propitiate Hari, the Lord of the Añjana mountain.
This wonderful hymn concerning the Lord of Veṅkaṭādri, composed by the noble Vādibhītikara, shines forth as a bond of devotion.
Thus ends the hymn to Añjanaśailanātha in its entirety.
